subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs where sender canonicalizes to destination_caller_id, should OpenClaw drop fail-closed when no distinct canonical peer can be recovered before access control?
rationale: That choice controls whether ambiguous local-sender payloads can reach authorization, pairing, routing, and reply delivery, so it is an identity-boundary policy decision rather than a purely mechanical refactor.

options.title: Repair Canonical Peers And Fail Closed
options.body: Use normalizeIMessageHandle for all comparisons, repair only a distinct canonical peer, and drop ambiguous local-sender payloads before access control when no peer is recoverable.

options.title: Repair Only When Confident
options.body: Use canonical comparison and repair distinct peers, but preserve current pass-through behavior for unrecoverable payloads while accepting the local-sender ambiguity risk.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: If the author’s remaining failure is a different root cause, pause this branch and track the narrower iMessage identity issue separately.

recommendation.title: Repair Canonical Peers And Fail Closed
recommendation.body: Use normalizeIMessageHandle for all comparisons, repair only a distinct canonical peer, and drop ambiguous local-sender payloads before access control when no peer is recoverable.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent destination_caller_id self-chat classification work is the closest merged history for this identity-boundary decision.
